coverage: Built from every page of the Parliament of Sri Lanka Acts listing (numbered Acts and Laws from 1948 to October 2026, Constitutional amendments, and the chapters of the 1956 Revised Legislative Enactments, filed as Ordinances unless an official text names them as Acts) and from about nine-tenths of the Department of Government Printing Acts listing (1980 to 2026). Of 1913 entries, 215 are in force, 81 repealed and 1617 unknown. A law is marked repealed only where the repeal section of a later Act, read in its official text on parliament.lk or documents.gov.lk, repeals it outright; repeals that take effect only from a date still to be appointed by Order, or that remove only some sections, are left unknown. A law is marked in force where an amending Act passed since 2000 names it as the principal enactment, or the Parliament listing records an amendment since 2000, and no Act in this index repeals it; yearly Appropriation and Finance Acts are not marked. 34 Revised Legislative Enactments chapters were confirmed by an official amending Act citing the Act by its chapter number and are now shown on the numbered Act, with the chapter entry removed. Still missing: LawNet's consolidated legislation could not be reached (its security certificate does not match its address), so no entry relies on it; most Acts before about 1995 exist only as scanned images, and only a few of their repeal sections were read; chapters with no amending Act since 1956 could not be matched to their original Act; and 277 amending Acts whose principal enactment is not in these listings are left out.

acts.sum: Sets 60 as the minimum age at which employers may retire workers, with limited grounds for earlier retirement.

acts.sum: Imposes income tax on individuals, companies, partnerships and other entities, and sets out how it is assessed and collected.

impl.sum: Every person chargeable with income tax must file returns, pay tax and instalments on time and keep records; the Commissioner-General of Inland Revenue administers the Act.

figs.l: company rate, as amended by No. 45 of 2022
top individual rate, as amended by No. 2 of 2025
maximum penalty for failing to register
cap on late-filing penalty per return
penalty on tax unpaid after 14 days
maximum fine for tax evasion

changes: Persons chargeable with income tax must register and file tax returns in the form the Commissioner-General specifies.
Income is taxed under employment, business, investment and other sources, at rates set in the First Schedule.
Late filing is penalised at the greater of 5% of tax owing plus 1% a month, or Rs. 50,000 plus Rs. 10,000 a month.
Underpayment caused by negligence or intent carries a penalty of 25%, or 75% in larger cases.
Proper documents must be kept; failing to keep them costs Rs. 1,000 a day after a warning notice.
Wilful evasion is an offence punishable by a fine up to Rs. 10 million, up to two years in prison, or both.
who: Employers and others who withhold tax
impl.when: in force since 1 April 2018; it repealed the Inland Revenue Act No. 10 of 2006
